- **Real impact often starts where access to healthcare is most limited. In my recent conversation on the Empowered Patient Podcast, we explored what it takes to bring innovation to settings where traditional structures around healthcare don’t easily reach the people we want to reach. It was particularly interesting to reflect on early experiences from different regions and what they teach us about designing innovative healthcare solutions. - **I've been reflecting on my first year as Head of Global Medical Affairs at Merz Therapeutics . What I have learned since joining – and what has genuinely surprised me – is how prominently Merz Therapeutic's core principle of ‘Better outcomes for more patients’ features in the work we do. Building Global Medical Affairs into a strategic pillar for the business through our ’one voice’ vision has been really important to me. It means creating a patient-focused framework that guides evidence generation and how we measure outcomes that truly matter to patients. A highlight of my time here so far was our recent global meeting, which brought together 70 team members from around the world. The energy in that room reminded me why our work matters. Through our function we have a unique opportunity to guide the organization with the mindset that the treatment is not the finish line. We have to keep asking what the other unmet needs are, what the patient's full journey looks like and who else is impacted. When a patient with spasticity can pick up a glass, comb their hair, or do up their buttons, that is the real impact. And it's not always something you can capture in a graph. #MerzTx #MedicalAffairs #PatientCentric #BetterOutcomesforMorePatients #SpecialtyNeurology ...more**

- **Reflecting on last week’s Medical Affairs Excellence Summit in Brussels, I left the meeting with a simple but powerful thought: progress starts with people! More specifically, when you see a team (or profession) genuinely moving forward, it’s always the people that are making it happen. This event may have been small, but the engagement was rich and meaningful, and it was highly rewarding to spend time in the company of motivated professionals from across the Medical Affairs space who all shared a common trait – a belief that “better” is achievable. The path we take through the various challenges in work (and in life) is almost always eased by human connection. These two days were a timely reminder that in an environment defined by increasing uncertainty, competitive pressures, and expectations, human connection provides a solid foundation from which Medical Affairs can grow. Grateful to my fellow panelists Selena Freisens, MD , Simon Messner, PhD and Thomas Lanz for a thoughtful discussion on the challenges and opportunities of incorporating real-world evidence – and to Marxo Smith for the opportunity to present our perspective on the commercial benefits of patient-partnered early-stage planning. More of these conversations, connections, and collaborations please – this is where progress gets amplified! #MedicalAffairs #PatientEngagement #EarlyStagePlanning #Strategy #Amiculum ...more ...more**

- **I am delighted to share that Merz has successfully completed its inaugural €450 million Schuldschein transaction. The debut transaction was signficantly oversubscribed and attracted strong interest across all investor groups. The successful placement represents an important milestone in the continued development of Merz’s financing strategy. It further diversifies our funding sources, broadens our investor base and strengthens the resilience and flexibility of our financing structure. Most importantly, it positions us well to support the future development of our business and provides additional financial flexibility to pursue both organic and inorganic growth opportunities. My sincere thanks go to all colleagues who contributed to this successful transaction through their expertise, commitment and teamwork. I would particularly like to acknowledge Karsten Kabas and Tobias Winkelmann, whose expertise, dedication and careful execution were instrumental in delivering this successful outcome. For me, this transaction is above all a strong vote of confidence in Merz, our strategy and our long-term prospects. It strengthens our financial flexibility, broadens our financing base and provides a solid foundation to support the continued growth and development of our business.**

- **„Wann haben Sie zuletzt etwas Neues gelernt?“ Ein echter OG im Recruiting – den ich selbst kaum noch stelle … aber aktuell ziemlich gerne beantworten würde. Also, falls mich jemand fragen würde, wäre das meine Antwort: Im Mai habe ich die Getting Things Done (GTD) Methode für Selbst‑ und Zeitmanagement gelernt – und ich bin ehrlich gesagt ein Fan-Girl geworden. Alle Aufgaben landen in einem zentralen System (bei mir: To-Do App) und werden von dort aus strukturiert, priorisiert und erledigt. Einmal konsequent umgesetzt, kann ich meine Arbeit deutlich besser einschätzen und bin tatsächlich entspannter. Keine Überraschung: Das System ist nur so gut wie die eigene Disziplin, es auch zu nutzen. Wiederrum eine Überraschung: Bunte Post-its haben gegen meine To-Do App endgültig verloren 😄 Und als kleiner Beweis für die Entspannung: Nach dem Workshop gab es noch einen richtig guten Abend mit den Kollegen 🍷 Wann habt ihr zuletzt wirklich etwas Neues gelernt – also so, dass ihr es direkt umgesetzt habt?**

- **Last week, I spent time at the SHRM Annual Conference in Orlando – one of the largest global gatherings of the HR community, bringing together executives, professionals, thought leaders, and experts from US and around the world. What made the experience particularly valuable were the many high-quality exchanges with fellow executives, international HR leaders, U.S. peers, and great speakers. Engaging across such a diverse and global set of perspectives as well as participating on panel discussions once again underlined how much our function benefits from open and cross-regional dialogue. What stood out is not a shift in direction — but the growing clarity and alignment around what many of us have been observing and actively shaping for some time: HR is no longer evolving into a business driver — it is expected to operate as one. As emphasized by SHRM CEO Johnny C. Taylor Jr., the connection between people strategy and business performance has become a defining standard. At Merz Therapeutics, this mindset has long been a core part of how we operate. As we continue to grow internationally, the real opportunity lies in consistently aligning people, culture, and business strategy globally and across regions. A particular highlight was the personal exchange with SHRM CEO Johnny C. Taylor Jr. — thank you Johnny for taking time and for the open and forward-looking conversation. Your perspective continues to shape the global HR agenda. Looking forward to continuing these conversations - and to further driving a globally connected, people and business-focused HR agenda at Merz Therapeutics. 👍 #SHRM26 #FutureOfWork #HRLeadership #GlobalHR #MerzTherapeutics #Leadership #PeopleStrategy**
